description:
Programme or Project Overview

The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at Utrecht University offers an internship placement (Internship Paard) focused on equine health. The internship gives students hands-on exposure to clinical work with horses within the faculty's equine clinic and teaching environment, one of Europe's leading veterinary schools.

Interns rotate through supervised activities in the equine clinic, supporting examinations, treatments and care routines while learning clinical protocols and patient handling. The placement is designed as a learning experience with structured supervision, and is suitable for veterinary students seeking clinical exposure in equine medicine as part of their study programme or between semesters.

Practical details

The internship position carries the standard internship allowance under university rules, and the working weeks follow the clinic's rota, including some weekend and evening duties under supervision. Applicants are enrolled in a veterinary or related study programme and can document their status at application. The vacancy closes on a fixed date, and candidates apply through the university's recruitment portal with a short motivation and CV.

Highlights

  • Hands-on clinical experience in equine health
  • Supervised rotations in the equine clinic
  • Exposure to examinations, treatment and care protocols
  • Structured supervision at a leading veterinary faculty
  • Internship allowance under university rules
  • Fixed closing date via the Utrecht recruitment portal

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
